igbinary.roundtrip.doc: igbinary_serialize($v), igbinary_unserialize of it, and igbinary_serialize of that: Rust reads what it writes back byte for byte

deviations.php: The second occurrence of the same array or object instance (a PHP reference, or a copy sharing its zend_array) is written as a back-reference (01-03, 22-24, 25).
deviations.reason: php_std::Value has no identity. Every empty array is written as the engine's shared immutable empty array (in full once, then as a back-reference), which is what PHP writes for data from literals, json_decode, unserialize and igbinary_unserialize; other arrays and objects are written in full. An empty array PHP built by unsetting elements, or returned by array_filter, is a separate instance there and written in full.

deviations.php: Back-references and PHP references become shared values or references; objects of other classes become __PHP_Incomplete_Class; recursive structures are recursive.
deviations.reason: Back-references and references read as copies (the value is equal; re-serializing writes them in full). Objects of classes other than stdClass, recursive structures and nesting deeper than igbinary::MAX_DEPTH (4096; PHP recurses until its stack runs out) fail with igbinary::Error::Unsupported.

deviations.php: igbinary_serialize, serialize and var_export of an object of another class (Utopia\Database\Document) write the object with its class name.
deviations.reason: An Extension value is written as its to_array() (getArrayCopy()), which is what PHP code stores (the cache stores getArrayCopy() of documents). json::encode writes it as an object, as json_encode does for an ArrayObject.
